correctness.rationale: A positive state-independent selection probability cancels in each stationary marginal equation; the finite chain is Feller on a compact cube. Positive lower bounds on branch probabilities give full support and an upper bound 2(1−q_0)^m on each point mass. The inverse branches induce doubling except at null endpoints. Both the branch kernel and doubling preserve the two Lebesgue decomposition types. Fourier invariance under doubling forces the absolutely continuous part, if any, to be proportional to Lebesgue, which is stationary for the logistic kernel only at β=0. For right endpoint cells I_m=F_+^m([-M,M]), stationarity and disjoint branches up to null boundaries give ν(I_m)=∫_{I_{m−1}}p_+(x)dν. Since |log p_+(x)−log q|≤2βM2^(−(m−1)) on I_{m−1}, the normalized ratios converge to one with summable geometric log errors. Equivalently the normalized branch product converges uniformly with omitted log tail bounded by 4βM2^(−m); this verifies the exact positive integral prefactor as well as its error. Reflection gives the left endpoint, and dyadic sandwiching gives the asserted logarithmic limits. At β=0 all dyadic masses are those of uniform measure.
residual_risks: No claim about peer interactions, finite-population mixing rates, or an unrestricted asymptotic equivalent at arbitrary nondyadic radii is certified.

evidence: Thiam's theorem states J_μσ=exp(P−φ) and the equivalent dual transfer condition. The pressure is zero for this normalized potential. Its Gibbs bounds give full support and μ([s^m]) comparable to q^m, already implying the endpoint exponent.
Jaroszewska–Rams supplies a Hausdorff-dimension upper bound, not this endpoint equivalent. Cao–Cortez treats fair signs/uniform Bernoulli convolution, not an own-opinion logistic law.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Ordinary Gibbs bounds alone do not establish a prefactor. The exact Jacobian part of the same broader characterization does give the needed recursion; with geometric variations this is enough for the prefactor and relative rate.

evidence: For ANY normalized two-branch Lipschitz g-function in this dyadic setting, exact inverse-branch change of variables gives μ([+^(m+1)])/μ([+^m])=E_μ[p_+(π X) | X∈[+^m]]. This is q+O(2^(−m)) since the cell diameter is 2M2^(−m). Summing the log errors gives μ([+^m])/q^m=A(1+O(2^(−m))) with A>0; iterating the same Jacobian identity gives A as the frozen normalized-product integral. The minus branch is identical with its own fixed-point weight.

Putting the prior model's p_+(M)=(1+exp(−βM))^(−1) into this generic formula supplies the exact exponent. The biased g-measure is ergodic by uniqueness of the equilibrium state in this setting and differs from the fair Bernoulli invariant measure, hence is singular to it; the direct Fourier proof in the record also works.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The only logistic-specific step in the sharp tail proof is evaluating a known branch probability at its attracting endpoint. The quantitative remainder follows by geometric summation of a Lipschitz bound, with no extra model-specific threshold or estimate. This is coverage by implication, not an allegation of verbatim duplication.

Agreement on n tail symbols bounds the variation of log p_s by 2βM2^(−n), making this a Lipschitz potential in the dyadic metric.

checked_sources: Frozen Finding and scope; exact Jacobian reduction above; Zheng–Porter §3 and affine singularity precedent.
value.rationale: Extreme opinions motivate the observable, but the advertised exponent is the standard fixed-point branch weight expressed in units of dyadic scale. The rate and integral prefactor are the generic geometric-distortion correction for any Lipschitz branch; the prefactor is not separately evaluated or used to prove a new property of the logistic model. The result resolves no further opinion-dynamics question outside that direct specialization, so the claim does not meet the standard for a worthwhile new exact invariant.
residual_risks: The model specialization can be pedagogically useful. This is not a claim that stationary tails with peer updates or other model-specific effects would be of low value.
